**By Government Decision, Legislative Changes Will Be Prepared for the Recognition of Diplomas Issued Before 2010**
10:44, 10.04.2026

By decision of the Government of Georgia, legislative changes will be submitted to Parliament, based on which the problems related to the recognition of diplomas issued before 2010 will be resolved for thousands of citizens – stated Givi Mikanadze, the Minister of Education, Science, and Youth of Georgia.

As the Minister noted, according to the change, 4-year full-time and 5-year part-time (distance) education will be recognized equally.

According to him, the change will affect students who enrolled in a university under a recognized regime but completed their studies under an unrecognized one, as well as citizens who were enrolled in universities by educational institutions before they obtained a license.

"We had this situation – our citizens were taking exactly the same number of subjects in 4-year programs and receiving the same qualification as in 5-year part-time programs. According to the legislation existing until now, the 5-year program was equated to a Master's degree, while the 4-year program was granted a Bachelor's degree. Based on the changes, those who completed a 4-year program will receive a diploma equated to a Master's degree, which will significantly facilitate the employment of citizens in their desired fields.

Before 2010, until a unified system was established, there was no registry in the field of education to ensure that students were informed. There were cases where specific universities, which had not been granted accreditation, did not inform applicants about this and enrolled them anyway. Subsequently, when they issued diplomas, graduates faced problems regarding the recognition of these documents.

Furthermore, a number of higher education institutions had authorization for a certain period, which was then terminated during the study period. Students were not informed about this either, and subsequently, these university graduates faced problems.

The presented legislative changes will finally put an end to the long, problematic processes that our citizens go through for diploma recognition – going to court, appealing processes, which is associated with time and effort. All of this will become a thing of the past once and for all, and the diplomas of thousands of our citizens will be recognized," stated Givi Mikanadze.
